data.gender_notes: Claus is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Norse name 'Klaus' or 'Klaeysa', meaning 'claw' or 'slave'. In Christian tradition, St. Nicholas of Myra, also known as Santa Claus, is the patron saint of children and gift-giving. This name evokes images of kindness, generosity, and faith. The name Claus carries the meaning “Famous as a slave” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Claus usually hope their child will grow to embody famous as a slave and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Claus total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.
